paragraphs: The following assessments concern mechanical door repairers' daily installation, inspection, repair, and testing work. They do not predict hiring, qualifications, licenses, authorization, or responsibility for on-site work safety.

Mechanical door repairers focus on installing and servicing automatic door mechanisms and hydraulic doors: assembling tracks and back hangs, positioning doors in openings, replacing worn or damaged parts and springs, adjusting opening and closing force, installing electric openers and photoelectric sensors, routing low-voltage wiring, and testing systems against drawings. Work often takes place outdoors and at heights, involves lifting heavy items such as door panels and using ladders and power tools, and requires following employer and authority safety procedures.

Entirely fictional task package: Provide a fictional door service work order, including 1 door type and opening dimension specification, 1 set of fictional track and spring component records, and 1 example of abnormal opening or closing force to assess. Within 60 minutes, write the inspection sequence, parts proposed for replacement or adjustment, opening and closing force and safety test points, and situations to escalate to authorized personnel. Do not use real customer or company data or others' unpublished materials.

Sample output and reflection: Check whether you first verified door type, opening, and drawings; explained the inspection sequence for tracks, hardware, springs, and electrical controls; provided opening and closing force and safety test records; and distinguished mechanical, electrical, and workplace safety controls. Then ask whether you can work outdoors and at heights, lift heavy door panels and safely use ladders and power tools, and follow authorization and safety procedures.

This page covers O*NET 49-9011.00 Mechanical Door Repairers: installing, servicing, or repairing automatic door mechanisms and hydraulic doors, including garage door mechanics. Common titles include commercial door installer, door installer, garage door installer, door repairer, and overhead door technician. Work mainly involves indoor and outdoor on-site installation and servicing, lifting door panels, working at heights, and using power tools. This page excludes adjacent occupations such as Electricians (47-2111.00), Glaziers (47-2121.00), and Carpenters.

entries: Work inputs: Automatic, hydraulic, and garage doors for installation or servicing; frames and tracks; springs and hardware; electric openers and photoelectric sensors; low-voltage wiring and distribution panels; drawings and schematics; ladders and scaffolding; power and hand tools; and employer and authority safety procedures.

Verifiable outputs: Properly installed doors with normal opening and closing force, assembled and secured tracks and back hangs, replaced or repaired springs and worn parts, routed and connected low-voltage wiring and electrical controls, service results recorded against work orders and drawings, and system operating records showing passed tests.

Complete workflow: Survey the site and assess opening conditions → check drawings and door type → install or secure tracks, back hangs, and frames → assemble doors and hardware and adjust force → install electric openers, photoelectric sensors, and low-voltage wiring → test the system, complete the work order, and hand over.

paragraphs: Work reality: Among U.S. O*NET respondents, 62% report daily outdoor exposure, 61% daily work at heights, and 65% typical workweeks exceeding 40 hours. These proportions do not cover every role. Work involves on-site lifting, tools, and customer communication. Check openings, drawings, track load-bearing capacity, controls, and power conditions. Stop when uncertain and refer to authorized personnel.

Environment and pace: O*NET respondents report 62% daily outdoor exposure, 61% daily work at heights, 88% daily use of common protective equipment, and 65% typical workweeks exceeding 40 hours. These describe U.S. respondents and cannot establish that most roles work in uncontrolled indoor settings or describe Chinese working hours.

Research inputs: 49-9011 tasks, context, education, RC, and Job Zone; 2025 wages and 2025–2035 projections. O*NET is a U.S. classification and cannot establish precisely equivalent Chinese qualifications or pay.

Check first: Site opening and door type, drawings and work requirements, track and load-bearing component condition, opening and closing force and control actions, low-voltage wiring and safety conditions, authorization scope, work order records, and handover requirements.

Work cycle: Survey the site and check drawings, install or secure tracks and doors, assemble hardware and adjust force, install controls and low-voltage wiring, test the system, and complete the work order and handover. Do not begin installation before confirming opening and safety conditions, or deliver before opening and closing force and electrical control tests pass.

Boundaries with adjacent roles: This page covers only installation and servicing of automatic and hydraulic doors, including garage doors, under 49-9011.00. Electricians (47-2111.00) handle regulated electrical wiring and power supply, Glaziers (47-2121.00) handle glass installation, and Carpenters build structural components. Authorization, power supply, and safety responsibilities are not interchangeable.

Difference from Electricians (47-2111.00): Electricians handle regulated wiring, power distribution, and supply. Mechanical door repairers handle mechanisms, tracks, hardware, and low-voltage control connections. Check authorized task allocation for judgments involving energized work or power systems.

Difference from Glaziers (47-2121.00): Glaziers select, cut, and install glass; mechanical door repairers handle door mechanisms and powered opening and closing. They often collaborate at the same opening but have different objects, tools, and acceptance criteria.

Difference from Carpenters: Carpenters build wooden structures and door and window frames; mechanical door repairers handle automatic and garage door mechanisms, hardware, and controls rather than structural construction.

Difference from Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters: Plumbers work on water supply, drainage, and piping systems; mechanical door repairers handle door mechanisms and controls. Before choosing this occupation, compare actual tasks, authorization, safety requirements, and progression paths rather than title similarity.

Task capabilities: AI task exposure for mechanical door repairers does not equal job replacement. Software can assist work order organization, scheduling, fault searches, and record drafting, but humans remain responsible for on-site judgment, power and load-bearing component safety judgments, authorization, and final delivery.

Editorial recommendation: Try work order records, parts list checks, and troubleshooting information searches. O*NET listings of work order and routing software do not prove generative AI adoption. Vendor demonstrations are not organizational adoption; authorized personnel retain on-site control.

Data and system prerequisites: Before adoption, check data, permissions, versions, and failure modes in work order software, equipment manuals, drawings, and parts lists. Judgments about door load-bearing capacity and energized work cannot rely solely on software output.

Human control: Qualified personnel must perform and review judgments involving power supply, energized work, load-bearing springs, and work at heights. Software output does not constitute safety permission.

Remaining responsibilities: Do not automate release for on-site safety judgments, handling energized and load-bearing components, system testing, or final delivery. No tool or system output constitutes an authorization decision.
Failure risks: Software or diagnostic outputs without on-site review may misguide part replacement or force adjustments, causing rework, equipment damage, or workplace safety incidents.

Employment evidence boundaries: Current materials mainly concern task-level exposure studies, such as the ILO 2025 Generative AI Exposure Index. They cannot establish this occupation's adoption rates, job cuts, or timelines. Task exposure, adoption, productivity, and employment measure different things.

Editorial recommendation: First trial verifiable work order drafting and searches. Authorized personnel must check door type, model-specific manuals, safety conditions, and test results for on-site servicing; software cannot release work.

Insufficient evidence: This page did not obtain a national occupational median wage for mechanical door repairers in mainland China. NBS2025 construction annual averages provide industry references for installation companies only; repair or sales companies require checks against their own industries. U.S. industry shares cannot establish Chinese classifications.

All are industry-level figures, not this occupation's median or starting pay.

Figures are independently rounded; do not recalculate by subtracting endpoints. The projection is not attributed to AI.

Wage statistical positions: These are U.S. national distributions. Percentiles do not represent seniority or experience levels. Average annual openings include replacement needs, not current vacancies or individual hiring probabilities.

Understanding these positions: Percentiles are distribution points, not promotion levels. Employment growth and average annual openings are different indicators and cannot replace each other. Industry and regional differences are substantial; do not extrapolate across regions.

Current O*NET industry page: Construction 72%, retail 18%, other 10%, describing U.S. employer distribution. Occupational industry wages were not obtained; national percentiles cannot fill industry values.

BLS2025–2035: From 28,400 to 30,300 employed, 6.4% growth, net growth of about 1,800, and 2,100 average annual openings. Endpoints and net growth are independently rounded. O*NET's 6% growth display is rounded. Openings include replacement and are not current hiring.
Task signal: Willing to work at heights and lift heavy door panels, safely use ladders, scaffolding, and power tools, and install and service according to procedures.
Task signal: Can read drawings and schematics, assess door types and installation methods against opening conditions, and precisely adjust opening and closing force with hand and power tools.
Task signal: Can identify worn or damaged door components, judge replacement or repair, and explain results and limitations.

The Big Five supports self-reflection only. Editorial observation suggestion: Check whether you review drawings, components, and test records item by item and promptly report uncertain conditions. Do not treat a conscientiousness label as occupational validity or qualification evidence.
Reasons for caution: If outdoor work, heights, heavy lifting, or patient tool use are difficult, first compare indoor roles or adjacent directions.

Reasons for caution: Interest assessments for mechanical door repairers support exploration only. Actual tasks, environments, qualifications, and learning costs still require verification; assessments cannot determine competence or qualifications.
Trial action: Use an entirely fictional door service work order to practice inspection, part replacement, and opening and closing force testing, and ask someone to review it.
RIASEC or personality frameworks can only help formulate questions. They cannot replace work samples, learning ability, qualifications, and actual performance evidence for mechanical door repairers.

Work at heights: Installing springs and tracks from ladders or scaffolding is triggered by unguarded elevated work, unsecured equipment, or lack of supervision. Falls may cause injury. Controls include using ladders and fall protection according to procedures, maintaining three points of contact, and having another person supervise. Boundaries are determined by employer safety procedures and responsible authorities.

Load-bearing springs and brackets: High tension may cause pinching or ejection injuries. DASMA recommends trained door-system personnel handle garage door spring and bottom bracket adjustments using model-specific manuals. Stop on abnormalities and refer to authorized personnel. This occupational page does not provide tension-release instructions.

Controls and wiring: Unclear power status or wiring may cause electric shock or equipment damage. Stop related steps and have authorized personnel isolate, verify, and handle the system under applicable electrical safety procedures. A single voltage check or after-the-fact confirmation cannot replace qualifications and safety controls.

Heavy lifting and tools: When lifting door panels, tracks, and heavy hardware, triggers include lifting excessive weight alone or improper posture. Muscle and lower-back injuries may result. Controls include lifting and handling aids, teamwork, and correct posture.

Shared escalation rule: If opening conditions, power status, load-bearing components, or safety conditions are unclear, stop related steps first. Under employer and authority procedures, hand over facts, impacts, and unresolved questions to an authorized responsible person.

Practical entry: Use only public or fictional data in entry-level mechanical door repair work samples to demonstrate site surveys, installation sequences, component judgments, and test records. First confirm first-year tasks and on-site safety supervision.

U.S.: BLS49-9011 typically indicates high school or equivalent, no related work experience, and moderate-term on-the-job training. O*NET respondents report 80% high school, 19% below high school, and 1% two-year degrees, not recruitment shares. In China, match actual voltage, activities, and construction-site categories to the 2026 special operations catalog. A door repairer title does not grant electrical work authority.

Work sample without experience: An entirely fictional door service work order. Within 60 minutes, write the inspection sequence, components proposed for replacement or adjustment, opening and closing force and safety test points, and escalation situations. Do not use real customer or company data.

Certification directories do not equal licenses, appointments, or signing authority. Match actual electrical, elevated, and construction activities to China's 2026 catalog. Employer permission does not replace statutory qualifications; learning records do not automatically grant operating authority.

Seven-day trial: Spend the first two days understanding door types and mechanisms, the next three completing a fictional work order inspection and adjustment exercise, the sixth having someone challenge conclusions, and the seventh documenting evidence to continue, stop, or change direction.

Qualification decision: O*NET's mechanical door repairer certification directory helps identify possible certificates, but certification does not equal a license, employer appointment, signing authority, or local authorization. Certificates, hiring, authorization, and signing responsibility are different statuses.

Capability progression: Before entering mechanical door repair, check official occupational scope, actual employer requirements, education or training, local qualifications, and supervised tasks. Do not infer these directly from adjacent occupations. Progression rests on verifiable work, not guaranteed years.

Transition pathway: List transferable capabilities such as site surveys, tool use, and mechanical judgment, along with required qualifications, tools, and responsibility experience. Check each against the adjacent role's authorization and safety requirements.

Current BLS U.S. 49-9011: About 28,400 employed in 2025, projected about 30,300 in 2035, with 6.4% growth, net growth of about 1,800, and 2,100 average annual openings. Figures are independently rounded. The overall projection is not attributed to AI or an individual's opportunities.

risks.mitigation: Use ladders and fall protection according to procedures and provide supervision.

risks.mitigation: Use handling aids, teamwork, and correct posture.

risks.consequence: May cause incorrect installation or workplace safety risks.
risks.mitigation: Verify the site and power first; stop and escalate under procedures.

description.text: Mechanical Door Repairers (O*NET 49-9011.00) install and service automatic and hydraulic doors, including garage doors. The 2025 BLS median annual wage was $55,720; employment was 28,400 in 2024, with projected faster-than-average growth of about 7% in 2024–2034. Includes work context, risks, and entry pathways.

subject.name: Mechanical Door Repairers
subject.summary: Mechanical Door Repairers (O*NET 49-9011.00) install and service automatic door mechanisms and hydraulic doors, including garage door mechanics: assembling tracks and back hangs, replacing springs and worn parts, adjusting opening and closing force, routing low-voltage wiring, and testing controls against drawings.
